name: Burn
label: Revelation
lede: Four songs on one Revelation seven-inch in 1990, with a swing and a stop-start menace nobody in New York hardcore had heard, and then twenty-seven years until the full-length.

eras.title: Four songs, fire and fusion
eras.text: By 1989 the youth crew sound had hardened into a formula. Gavin Van Vlack, out of Side by Side and Absolution, wanted a band that swung, and he found a singer in Chaka Malik who could ride it. One seven-inch later, New York hardcore had a new way to move.

years.h: Van Vlack talks them into it
years.p: Gavin recruits Chaka and drummer [[Alan Cage|65d4abbb-054b-4106-a826-0cb2b306341e]] of Beyond, with Alex Napack of [[Pressure Release|d129edff-83d0-4d95-976c-87b6a2dd57fd]] on bass. Napack gets credit for the name. An earlier drummer, John Krisciun, came before Cage.

q: It was so lawless, that you could really do anything.
years.src: No Echo (Gavin Van Vlack interview) · The Hundreds
years.h: South Williamsburg practice, Lower East Side stages
years.p: They rehearse in South Williamsburg and play CBGB, the Pyramid Club and ABC No Rio, in a city Van Vlack remembers as wide open.
years.xp:
Van Vlack's road to Burn was rough. He told No Echo his family moved to New York from New Hampshire when his mother needed cancer treatment at Sloan Kettering; he landed in foster care, and from 15 on he slept in abandoned buildings and on friends' floors, with [[Porcell|dff848b4-bb79-445a-81e1-3db65b7ddd3e]] of [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] sometimes sneaking him into his parents' house.

Before hardcore there was graffiti: he wrote NATZ with the SPORTS crew in the eighties. The son of a Mexican mother and a Dutch father, he's said both sides of the family were hostile to the mix. That street-level looseness came onto the stage with him.

years.p: Four songs. Chaka came up with the cover concept. Writer Anthony Pappalardo heard fire and fusion, pounding the pavement like demo-era [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]]. Revelation's own page calls it groundbreaking.
years.xp: What set it apart was the rhythm: swing and sudden dynamic drops where other bands just went faster. Revelation's catalog lists a first run split between black and pink vinyl, and the record has been repressed ever since.

years.p: The drummer joins [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]]' new band, and Burn can't find anyone who plays at his level.

eras.title: Greenpoint, and a record that waited a decade
eras.text: Without Cage the band kept writing, moved to Greenpoint, and recorded in 1992. Then it ended, and the members scattered into the noisier, heavier bands of the nineties.

years.p: New songs taped in 1992, when, in Chaka's words, nothing in their new Brooklyn base was established yet. They'd sit on a shelf for ten years.
Chaka starts [[Orange 9mm|66ae7e89-680b-4f0f-a990-8a4e0bdf3d51]]. Van Vlack goes on to [[Die 116|59ff819b-b635-473d-ba52-f61d44835bd7]], Pry and The Big Collapse.

eras.title: Cleanse
eras.text: A short return in 1998 grew into a new line-up with Vic DiCara, of Inside Out and 108, on second guitar. Two releases came out of it, one brand new, one ten years old.

years.p: Burn plays again, for the first time since the split.
Chaka and Gavin with Vic DiCara on second guitar and Manny Carrero, later of [[Glassjaw|429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed]], on bass.
Revelation releases the recordings the band made just before breaking up.

eras.title: The word is real
eras.text: Twenty-five years after the seven-inch, Burn came back as a working band rather than a reunion act. New players, new records, and in 2017 the first full-length they'd ever made.

years.cap: Black N' Blue Bowl, New York, May 2015
q: The word that comes to mind, is real.
years.src: No Echo · Black N' Blue Productions · Brooklyn Vegan
years.h: Special guest at the Black N' Blue Bowl
years.p: Burn is added as an exclusive appearance at the New York hardcore festival's May weekend, with [[Durijah Lang|42c3124a-fa12-4e3f-a373-6bc155dd416f]] on drums and Carrero on bass. Chaka's summary of what the band was about:
years.xp: Chaka said the plan was to play more in the style of the original four-song seven-inch rather than chase the later records.

years.p: A London show on October 4, then Santa Ana, Berkeley and Los Angeles from October 9 to 11.
The first new Burn music in fifteen years.
Twenty-eight years after they started, on Deathwish Inc., produced by [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] and mastered by Howie Weinberg.
